Based on the astronomical data you provided, the short answer is: **It is highly unlikely that you would be able to see the Moon with your naked eyes right now.**

Here is the breakdown of why it will likely remain "invisible" to you:

### 1. The "Washout" Effect (Solar Proximity)
The most significant factor is that the Moon is only **14.173 degrees** away from the Sun. In observational astronomy, this is considered very close. Because the Sun is currently at an altitude of nearly 19 degrees, it is still high enough in the sky to flood the atmosphere with light. This creates a massive amount of "sky glow" or atmospheric scattering. Even though the Moon is technically above the horizon, it is sitting in the "glare" of the Sun's proximity.

### 2. The Phase (Waxing Crescent)
You mentioned the Moon is only **1.53% illuminated**. At this phase, the Moon is a very thin, tiny sliver. A sliver that small is extremely difficult to distinguish from the surrounding bright daylight sky, especially when it is positioned so close to the Sun.

### 3. Contrast
For an object to be visible to the unaided eye, there must be enough contrast between the object and the background. Because the sky brightness is "bright daylight" and the Moon is so small and close to the Sun, the contrast is almost zero. The Moon will be "lost" in the brightness of the sky.

### Summary
While your app correctly identifies that the Moon is physically above the horizon, the **atmospheric conditions** (daylight brightness) and the **geometry** (proximity to the Sun) work in your favor. 

**Verdict:** You can breathe a sigh of relief. Unless you have high-powered binoculars or a telescope to cut through the glare, the Moon will be effectively invisible to you right now.
